purpose: Penciclovir is a cream used to treat cold sores (fever blisters) caused by the herpes simplex virus that appear on or around the lips. It helps cold sores heal faster and reduces pain and discomfort. It works best when you start using it as soon as you feel the tingling or burning that signals a cold sore is coming.
how_it_works: The herpes virus needs to make copies of itself to cause a cold sore. Penciclovir works by blocking a key tool the virus uses to reproduce, called DNA polymerase. By interfering with this process, the virus cannot multiply as easily, which helps your body fight it off faster and shortens how long the cold sore lasts.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is a mild headache. At the site where you apply the cream, you might notice temporary redness, mild burning or stinging, numbness, or skin irritation. These effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Only use this cream on your lips and the skin around your mouth — never put it inside your mouth, nose, eyes, or on your genitals. Avoid getting it in your eyes as it can cause irritation. If you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have a weakened immune system, talk to your doctor before using this medication. It does not cure herpes and will not prevent you from spreading the virus to others.
typical_dosing: Apply a small amount of the cream directly to the cold sore every 2 hours while you are awake, for 4 days in a row. Start using it as soon as you notice the first signs of a cold sore for the best results. Wash your hands before and after applying the cream.
